claims.summary: Astrid reports that an awaited telemetry handler may create backlog or delay shutdown when integration work becomes expensive.
claims.disposition: Retain the concern as primary architectural evidence. Current timing diagnostics make it observable but do not declare the scheduling risk absent.

claims.summary: Telemetry integration currently runs sequentially in the WebSocket receive loop.
claims.disposition: Verified from the complete source: decode, derivation, throttled artifact scan, state update, persistence, and trace work complete before the loop receives the next frame.

claims.summary: The bridge needs evidence that separates handler pipeline cost from lock contention.
claims.disposition: Verified existing telemetry_integration_health_v1 observations for pre-write pipeline, write-lock wait, and write-lock hold with latest, EWMA, and maximum values; the focused test passed.

claims.summary: Reconnect after WebSocket failure and ping-to-pong handling should be covered.
claims.disposition: Verified capped/resettable shutdown-aware backoff and source-level ping/pong routing. Two backoff tests and the mock WebSocket receive integration test passed.

claims.summary: The telemetry handler should be moved to an offloaded worker to prevent receive-loop delay.
claims.disposition: Preserve as an exact Tier 5 wait. A worker changes live sensory ordering, buffering, backpressure, and cadence and therefore requires bounded runtime evidence, a scoped approval, capacity and drop policy, canary, and rollback.
